extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Exchange administrators, health insurers/issuers, agents/brokers, health policy stakeholders, and public commenters on the proposed CMS/HHS rule
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and evaluate the standards, methodological assumptions, and proposed regulatory changes in the CMS proposed rule concerning Exchange eligibility, verification, enrollment processes, premium measures, and program integrity. Useful for preparing informed notice-and-comment submissions or compliance planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 1-year ACS microdata to estimate eligible populations
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of State residents in the 100-150 percent FPL income range who are potentially eligible for Exchange coverage in each year is estimated using the 2019 and 2023 1-year ACS files from IPUMS USA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodology provides a current portrait of residents meeting the 100-150 percent FPL criteria in each year but leads to less precise estimates than multi-year ACS samples with larger sample sizes. Comments sought on improvements including use of multi-year ACS samples or refinement of measures of income and family unit to more closely align with Exchange premium tax credit (PTC) eligibility (MAGI-based).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'potentially eligible' population (100-150% FPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: State residents ages 19-64 with household incomes between 100-150 percent FPL who are not enrolled in Medicaid or Medicare are considered potentially eligible for Exchange coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows prior methodology and excludes children age 18 and under who are eligible for Medicaid/CHIP if incomes are in this range, and adults 65+ who are likely eligible for Medicare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust 2023 ACS estimates to 2024 using state-level population change
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the 2024 ACS microdata is not yet available, the number of individuals potentially eligible for Exchange coverage in 2024 was estimated by applying State-level estimates of population change from 2023 to 2024 from the U.S. Census Bureau to the 2023 ACS estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adjustment assumes that changes in population within the 100-150 percent FPL range are similar to those within the State and ignores potential distributional changes; methodology limitations and exclusions (Minnesota, New York, Oregon due to BHP; District of Columbia due to insufficient OEP PUF income info; Idaho 2019 not reported) are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of Exchange 'take-up' rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Take-up is calculated by dividing Exchange enrollment for each State by the corresponding estimate of eligible State residents from the ACS and multiplying by 100.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While useful for trend analysis and cross-State patterns, these estimates should not be interpreted as precise measures because: (1) use of 1-year ACS samples reduces precision vs multi-year samples; (2) Census poverty definition differs from MAGI used for PTC eligibility (differences in income sources and household composition); (3) ACS timing (asks about prior 12 months) does not align with calendar/plan year income; (4) survey income underreporting; (5) eligible population estimates may include individuals not eligible for subsidized Exchange coverage (those with affordable employer coverage, unreported Medicaid, non-lawfully present immigrants, VA enrollees); and (6) estimates may exclude certain eligible enrollees included in enrollment counts (e.g., some 65+ who do not qualify for premium-free Medicare).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and explain causes of take-up rates exceeding 100%
rubrics_metrics.description: High take-up rates (exceeding 100%) may reflect imprecision or measurement differences, but can also indicate misestimation or improper enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible explanations listed include imprecise population estimates, income measurement differences, people misestimating income at enrollment, failure to update income when auto re-enrolled (using prior-year verified income), intentional overstatement of income to qualify for subsidies, or agent/broker/web-broker improper enrollments. Observed extreme cases (e.g., Florida 438% in 2024) suggest causes beyond sampling imprecision. Noted correlation with non-expansion Medicaid states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper-bound estimation of erroneous/improper enrollments by summing excess enrollments
rubrics_metrics.description: One approach to estimate reduction in erroneous/improper enrollments is to sum total enrollments in 2024 that exceed 100 percent of potential enrollees (from Table 15), yielding as many as 4.4 million erroneous or improper enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is treated as an upper-bound estimate. Reasons why it may overestimate include recent CMS actions to suspend agents/brokers, attribution of all excess to error without accounting for income uncertainty or ACS imprecision. It could also underestimate if improper enrollments exist in States with take-up below 100%. CMS acknowledges uncertainty and seeks comment on improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling assumptions for projected enrollment, premiums, and APTC impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Projections start with internal CMS monthly enrollment, premium, and APTC data summarized as average monthly amounts and trended using historical patterns and projected growth in the under-65 population and NHEA less Medicare for spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key assumptions include: IRA subsidy expiration after PY2025 reducing fully-subsidized plans; assumption ~42% of recent enrollment growth will discontinue coverage after expiration; expected 750,000–2,000,000 fewer enrollees in 2026 if proposals finalized; claims impact to risk pool range -0.5% to +4%; combined estimated decreases include 3.4% from removing monthly 150% FPL SEP, 0.5% SEP verification effect, 1% AV change effect; pricing assumed to 84% loss ratio to compute revised PMPMs; APTCs assumed 88.8% of premium PMPM; APTC enrollment assumed 90.6% of total; premium growth and enrollment growth rates for 2027-2029 provided. CMS recognizes uncertainty and seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to remove §147.104(i) (attribution of payment of premium to past-due premiums)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing the current prohibition on an issuer attributing payment of premium for new coverage to past-due premiums owed for prior coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: allowing issuers (as permitted by State law) to condition sale of new coverage on payment of past-due premiums could improve the risk pool by promoting continuous coverage without imposing significant financial burden for most people who owe past-due premiums. Alternative of no action (maintaining broad enrollment rights) was considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to revise definition of 'lawfully present' to exclude DACA recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose adjusting the definition of 'lawfully present' used for QHP/BHP eligibility to exclude DACA recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative considered: fully revert to pre-2024 definition, but that would undo technical/clarifying changes and affect small distinct groups that generally entered with inspection and can adjust status. CMS chose to exclude DACA recipients while retaining other technical clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to allow Exchanges to remove APTC after one year of FTR (modify §155.305(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify rule to allow Exchanges to remove APTC after an enrollee or their tax filer has been identified as failing to file and reconcile APTC for one tax year (currently two consecutive years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: failing-to-file-and-reconcile (FTR) serves as a check on improper enrollments and helps protect low-income consumers from large unexpected tax liabilities. Considered alternative: no action (keep two-year requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require Exchanges to generate annual income inconsistencies in specific income ranges (§155.320(c)(3)(iii) amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add amendments specifying that Exchanges must generate annual income inconsistencies when a tax filer's attested projected annual income is ≥100% and ≤400% FPL and trusted data sources indicate projected income is under 100% FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: concerns applicants inflating incomes or applications being submitted on their behalf with inflated incomes; carrying out alternative income verification in this scenario may limit tax filers' potential reconciliation liability. CMS considered no action but proposes the inconsistency-generation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove §155.320(c)(5) (do not accept attestations when IRS confirms no tax return data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing the current requirement that Exchanges accept attestations and not set an Income DMI when the IRS confirms there is no such tax return data available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: removing this provision is crucial for program integrity; benefit outweighs the administrative burden of requiring an Income DMI when IRS lacks tax return data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove automatic 60-day extension in §155.315(f)(7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing the provision requiring applicants to receive an automatic 60-day extension in addition to the current 90 days for providing documentation to verify household income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: align with the 90-day statutory period and reduce continued APTC beyond the statutory timeframe; administrative burden and taxpayer costs outweigh benefits identified in 2024 Payment Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require reducing APTC so enrollee owes $5 monthly when not reapplying (§155.335(a)(3) and (n))
rubrics_metrics.description: Add §155.335(a)(3) and (n) to require that when an enrollee does not submit an application for updated eligibility on or before the last day to select a plan for Jan 1 coverage and the enrollee's portion of the premium would be $0 after APTC, Exchanges must decrease the APTC such that the remaining monthly premium owed equals $5 for the first month and every following month the enrollee does not confirm/update eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative methods like outreach or automatically re-enrolling without APTC were considered; CMS determined $5 residual premium strikes a balance between prompting action and avoiding undue hardship and destabilizing the risk pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and rejection of auto re-enrollment without any APTC
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considered modifying annual redetermination to auto re-enroll an enrollee without any APTC if they did not submit an updated application, but rejected it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale for rejection: would create undue financial hardship, be a barrier to coverage, risk losing lower-risk enrollees who are least likely to actively re-enroll (destabilizing market and increasing premiums/uninsured rates). Comments from 2021 Payment Notice influenced the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of the bronze-to-silver crosswalk policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2024 Payment Notice allowed Exchanges to move CSR-eligible enrollees from a bronze QHP into a silver QHP if the silver had a lower or equivalent net premium post-APTC with same provider network; CMS considered leaving it but proposes rescinding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: consumers and assisters are largely aware of more generous subsidies today; the policy may confuse consumers, undermine choice, and create unexpected tax liability. CMS believes benefits no longer outweigh harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove flexibilities in §155.400(g) for fixed-dollar or gross-premium percentage binder thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing flexibilities that would allow issuers to adopt a fixed-dollar premium payment threshold or a gross premium-based percentage payment threshold for binding payment (binder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: both fixed-dollar and gross-premium percentage thresholds can present program integrity risks by allowing consumers (and improperly-enrolled Medicaid beneficiaries) to remain in coverage longer than intended and accrue premium debt; issuers may instead implement existing net premium percentage-based policy allowing consumers who pay majority of premium to avoid grace period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorten Open Enrollment Period (OEP) end date to December 15 nationally
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose that the OEP for all Exchanges ends on December 15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered alternatives included maintaining length, providing state flexibility, or moving OEP to March 1–April 15 to minimize adverse selection and maximize choice. Rejected changes due to concern about market disruption; CMS prioritizes reducing adverse selection and premium growth over additional enrollment time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal monthly 150% FPL SEP under §155.420
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose fully repealing the monthly 150 percent FPL Special Enrollment Period (SEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: fully subsidized plans create opportunities for agents/brokers/web-brokers to improperly enroll people (commission capture) and for consumers to falsely represent income; consumers at/below 150% FPL may wait to enroll until care needed, destabilizing risk pool. CMS concludes benefits of increased access do not outweigh higher premiums and program integrity risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require pre-enrollment SEP verification for most SEP categories on Federal platform (§155.420 amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing the Federal platform limitation that pre-enrollment verifications are only for loss of minimum essential coverage, to allow pre-enrollment verification for most SEP categories for Exchanges on the Federal platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the risk of enrolling ineligible individuals outweighs administrative burden; increased verification helps limit improper enrollments and protect consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require Exchanges to verify at least 75% of new SEP enrollments for consumers not already enrolled
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose that all Exchanges, including State Exchanges, must conduct pre-enrollment SEP verification for at least 75 percent of new enrollments through SEPs for consumers not already enrolled in coverage through the applicable Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: standardizing SEP verification across Exchanges reduces risk and protects consumers, while 75% threshold allows flexibility since it's not cost-effective for each State to verify all SEP types. CMS seeks comment on whether to require verification for most SEP types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change premium measure used in premium adjustment percentage (§156.130)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose changing the premium measure used in the premium adjustment percentage calculation to use a private health insurance premium measure (excluding Medigap and property and casualty insurance) instead of NHEA employer-sponsored insurance-only estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal would include only premiums for employer-sponsored insurance and direct purchase insurance (excluding Medigap and P&C). Rationale: better reflect premium trends in private health insurance market since 2013. CMS seeks comment on data source and whether to use average per enrollee private health insurance premiums or continue using employer-sponsored insurance premiums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) small entity analysis criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For RFA purposes, 'small entity' analysis treats health insurance issuers under NAICS 524114 (Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers) with SBA size standard of $47M annual receipts; some issuers could be classified under 621491 (HMO Medical Centers) with $44.5M standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes few comprehensive health issuers fall below thresholds; based on MLR data ~84 of 479 issuers had revenue ≤ $47M, many of which belong to larger holding groups. CMS anticipates small issuers could be impacted but cannot quantify due to uncertainty (market share, holding group membership, enrollment, risk mix). Seeks comment on estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) threshold consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: UMRA requires assessing costs/benefits for rules imposing spending > $100M in 1995 dollars (≈ $187M in 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not all costs quantified, CMS expects combined impact on State/local/Tribal governments and private sector does not meet UMRA definition of an unfunded mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism consultation and State flexibility considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 13132 requirements: consult with States when issuing proposed/final rules that may have federalism implications; CMS engaged with NAIC and State insurance officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS attempted to balance State interests in regulating issuers with need for market stability. States retain Exchange design flexibility and are not required to establish an Exchange. Some initial Exchange development funded by planning grants; Exchanges must be financially self-sustaining thereafter. Comments sought and intergovernmental engagement noted.
